drivingQuestion: Does the mishna's first clause follow the Rabbis or R' Meir?
outcomeNote: Rav's correction stands; Rav Ḥinnana's reasoning is rejected

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא לְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב: לֹא יַעֲמוֹד אָדָם בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וּמְטַלְטֵל בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שָׁבְקַתְּ רַבָּנַן וְעָבְדַתְּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר?!
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Rav Ḥinnana bar Shelamiya would teach» this mishna «to Ḥiyya bar Rav before Rav» as follows: «A person» may «not stand in a private domain and move» objects that are «in a public domain.» Rav «said to him:» Have «you abandoned» the majority opinion of «the Rabbis and followed» the solitary dissenting opinion of «Rabbi Meir,» who is stringent in this regard?

segments.he: הוּא סָבַר: מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, רֵישָׁא נָמֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וְלָא הִיא: סֵיפָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְרֵישָׁא רַבָּנַן.
segments.en: The Gemara explains: Rav Ḥinnana «maintains that from» the fact that «the latter clause» of the mishna, was taught in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Meir,» it can be inferred that «the first clause» was «likewise» taught in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Meir. But» in fact «that is not so: The latter clause» is in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Meir, while the first clause» is in accordance with that of «the Rabbis.»
